comments.body:
## Root cause NOT proven — ticket stays OPEN. Mechanism proven, runner trigger not.

Per the "no guess-patch" rule this is evidence, not a fix. Two hypotheses in the original
write-up are **refuted**, one new latent bug is **proven**, and the remaining candidate is
strongly corroborated but unreproduced.

### The exact invocation

`src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py:248`, in `_publish_and_prune`:

    create = _git(base_path, "bundle", "create", bundle_path, "HEAD", f"refs/heads/{ref}")

`_git` -> `gitutil.run_git` -> plain `subprocess.run`. **No retry wrapper is in this path at
all** — not `_with_index_lock_retry`, not `_with_transient_head_retry`, not the per-store
advisory git-op lock. The whole `s3_doctor` module sits outside rebar's self-healing git seam.

### What `fatal: bad object HEAD` actually means (proven by experiment)

| repo state | git's message |
|---|---|
| unborn HEAD | `fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD': unknown revision …` |
| HEAD symref -> missing branch | `fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD': …` |
| HEAD resolves, **loose object removed** | `fatal: bad object HEAD` <- exact CI match, single line |
| object file present but empty | `error: object file … is empty` x3, then `fatal: bad object HEAD` |
| object corrupt | `error: inflate: data stream error` / `fatal: loose object … is corrupt` |

So `bad object` is git's `get_reference()` path: the name resolved to an OID but
`parse_object()` returned NULL. It means **the object was unreadable**, not that a rev was
unresolvable.

- **REFUTED: "the literal `HEAD` argument failed to resolve."** An unborn or dangling HEAD
  produces `ambiguous argument`, never `bad object`. Also, `HEAD` is merely the FIRST rev
  argument — with the object missing, bundling `refs/heads/tickets` alone dies with
  `fatal: bad object refs/heads/tickets`. The word HEAD in the message carries no information.
- **REFUTED: "`b41953…` in the message proves the object existed."** `git rev-parse HEAD`
  prints the sha by reading the ref file even when the object is absent, so `_fold_heads`'
  `rev-parse` would have returned it either way.
- **PROVEN: the object was ABSENT, not empty or corrupt.** The empty and corrupt cases emit
  extra `error:` lines first; the CI stderr was the single `fatal:` line, and the full job log
  greps clean for `object file … is empty`, `is corrupt`, `unable to unpack`, `inflate`.

### Mechanism reproduction

Running the real `heal_multi_bundle` against the real harness with `s3_doctor._git` wrapped to
delete the merge commit's loose object immediately before the bundle call:

    could not bundle merged tip ad862009255c3e329ae103e80fd2430ac6bbe95a for ref tickets: fatal: bad object HEAD

Byte-for-byte the CI shape. This proves the mechanism (object absent from the ODB at bundle
time). It does **not** prove what made it absent on the runner.

### What is ruled out as the trigger

- **Background auto-gc/repack.** Instrumented a real heal run: the healed tracker has **2 loose
  objects and 1 pack**, against `gc.auto` 6700 and `gc.autoPackLimit` 50. Auto-gc cannot fire.
  (Worth noting separately: this ad-hoc test clone has `gc.autoDetach` at its default `true`,
  because rebar's `init._gc_config_unit` ensure — the ADR 0051 / bug 88eb remediation forcing
  foreground gc — never runs on a test-created clone. Not the trigger here, but the protection
  rebar built for its own stores is absent in these fixtures.)
- **Leaked `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` / `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`.** No test writes git env
  vars into `os.environ`; a leak would also have applied to the merge, not just the bundle.
- **Cross-test interference.** Every scenario builder uses its own `tmp_path`. The failing test
  is functionally identical to its four passing siblings apart from a pass-through `write_lock`
  spy — which itself argues the flake could have landed on any of them.
- **Local reproduction: 0 failures in 27 runs** (15 serial with `-p no:randomly`, 12 under
  `-n 4`).

### Remaining candidate (suspected, unproven)

A runner-side transient object-DB availability blip. Corroborated by three documented instances
of the same class in this repo, all on the same runner fleet:
- `gitutil.py` `_TRANSIENT_HEAD_MARKERS` — `could not parse HEAD`, bug childsafe-special-springtail,
  "a runner-FS read hiccup, NOT data corruption… the identical invocation succeeds on retry".
- `event_append.py` `_TRANSIENT_ADD_MARKERS` — the write-side object-DB transient.
- `event_append.py` `_INVALID_OBJECT_MARKERS`, bug 4c1c — "a loose object that vanished between
  `git add` and `git commit` — a background gc repack, **or a partial object write under FS/memory
  pressure**". That is literally this vanished-object case, already observed in production here.

Strong prior art is not proof, so no retry is being added on this evidence.

### If this recurs, the next step is bounded and specific

1. Route `s3_doctor._git` through the existing `gitutil` self-healing seam instead of raw
   `run_git`, so it inherits the lock retry and transient-marker family rather than growing a
   fourth private copy. `git bundle create` mutates no store state — it reads objects and writes
   a scratch file the caller re-creates and deletes — so it satisfies the same idempotency
   precondition `_with_transient_head_retry` documents.
2. If a marker is added, scope it to the missing-object family and distinguish it in the raised
   error: `S3DoctorConflict(... "heads conflict; run rebar fsck-recover")` misdescribes an ODB
   read failure, and its hint is the wrong advice for a merge that never conflicted.

### Separately PROVEN latent bug (not this failure) — filed as its own ticket

When `current_branch != ref` — a detached HEAD, a differently-checked-out branch, or a
bare/mirror tracker — line 248 still bundles the literal `HEAD`, which then names an unrelated
commit (silently bundling the wrong tip) or dies `ambiguous argument 'HEAD'` on an unborn HEAD.
The `HEAD` argument IS load-bearing: a bundle containing only `refs/heads/tickets` clones with
`warning: remote HEAD refers to nonexistent ref, unable to checkout` and no commits, which would
break `s3_doctor_harness.healed_tip`. So the fix is to make HEAD explicit and correct, not to
drop it.

### On the "shared trigger with bug ac76" note

Both did fail in run 31349549323, but in **different jobs** (this one in the py3.11 integration
phase, ac76 in the py3.13 unit phase). ac76 has since been root-caused to a shared-index commit
race entirely inside its own test, with no runner-resource component. So the two are NOT one
mechanism. The only shared factor is that a loaded xdist runner widens pre-existing windows.

    tests/integration/test_s3_doctor.py::test_heal_collapses_two_bundles_losslessly
    S3DoctorConflict: could not bundle merged tip 0d61f26d17bbec57e3fd48ef27fbe8bec3d1130d for ref tickets: fatal: bad object HEAD

Third recorded occurrence and the THIRD distinct sibling test (after test_heal_runs_merge_under_write_lock on run 31349549323 and test_heal_is_crash_idempotent on run 31340000912), confirming this ticket's own prediction that the flake 'could have landed on any of them'.

The change under test only adds pytest --timeout flags to external/offline CI lanes and extends a workflow-parity unit test. It touches no src/, not _build-and-test.yml (which owns the failing integration tier), and nothing this test exercises. Only one commit has ever touched s3_doctor.py or its tests (2d440ad668, 2026-08-08), so the code is byte-identical across all three failures and a regression is not possible.

Reproduction attempts on that tree, all green: the test alone 4x; the full integration tier under CI's exact -n 4 --dist loadgroup config (155 passed, 5 skipped). Consistent with the 0/27 recorded here.

Also corroborates the missing-object family rather than an unborn HEAD: run 31340000912 raised the same fault with the SHA named directly ('bad object ae7d19a6...'), so the literal HEAD token in the message carries no information.

# `s3_doctor` sits outside rebar's self-healing git seam, so a transient object-DB read fails the heal

## Proven mechanism

Three CI occurrences (runs 31340000912, 31349549323, 31558315198 — three DIFFERENT sibling
tests) fail identically:

    S3DoctorConflict: could not bundle merged tip <sha> for ref tickets: fatal: bad object HEAD

The investigation on this ticket established, by experiment against real git:

- `fatal: bad object` is git's `get_reference()` path — the name resolved to an OID but
  `parse_object()` returned NULL, i.e. **the object was unreadable at that instant**. An unborn
  or dangling HEAD produces `ambiguous argument`, never `bad object`; an empty or corrupt object
  emits extra `error:` lines the CI logs do not contain. So the object was ABSENT, not corrupt.
- The literal `HEAD` token in the message carries no information: run 31340000912 raised the
  same fault with the SHA named directly (`bad object ae7d19a6…`).
- The mechanism reproduces byte-for-byte by making the merge commit's object unreadable
  immediately before the bundle call.
- **`src/rebar/_store/s3_doctor.py`'s `_git` helper calls `gitutil.run_git` directly.** No retry
  wrapper is in that path at all — not `_with_index_lock_retry`, not
  `_with_transient_head_retry`, not the per-store advisory git-op lock. The whole `s3_doctor`
  module is the one store git caller OUTSIDE rebar's self-healing seam, while every other store
  write path routes through `gitutil.run_git_write` and self-heals exactly this class of
  runner-FS read blip.

The runner-side TRIGGER (what made the object briefly unreadable) remains unproven and is NOT
in scope. What is in scope is the proven structural gap: the same fault class that the rest of
the store rides out unassisted is fatal here, and it has now cost three review cycles.

## Scope — reuse the existing seam, do not grow a fourth private retry

1. Route `s3_doctor._git` through the existing `gitutil.run_git_write` seam instead of raw
   `run_git`, so it inherits the per-store advisory git-op lock, the bounded index/ref-lock
   retry, and the transient read-fault retry. `git bundle create` reads objects and writes a
   scratch file the caller re-creates and deletes; the other doctor invocations are reads,
   merges and scratch-ref updates. All satisfy the idempotency precondition
   `_with_transient_head_retry` documents.
2. Extend the existing transient-marker family in `gitutil` to the PROVEN missing-object
   signature (`bad object`) so the observed fault self-heals, keeping the marker set tight and
   greppable exactly as `_TRANSIENT_HEAD_MARKERS` is. No new retry loop, no new backoff policy,
   no new module — the existing wrapper gains one scoped marker.
3. Distinguish the failure in the raised error: `S3DoctorConflict`'s default hint ("tickets
   store heads conflict; run: rebar fsck-recover") misdescribes an object-DB read failure on a
   merge that never conflicted, and sends the operator to the wrong tool.

This is behavior-preserving hardening justified by recurrence: a success or any non-transient
failure still returns at once, so a genuine error surfaces unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `s3_doctor._git` routes through `gitutil.run_git_write`; no raw `run_git` call remains in
      `s3_doctor`.
- [ ] The proven `bad object` signature is retried by the existing transient-read wrapper in
      `gitutil`, scoped to that marker family — no new retry loop is introduced.
- [ ] A test injects the transient deterministically (first bundle attempt fails with the exact
      CI signature, the identical retry succeeds) and asserts the heal completes losslessly.
      It fails before the change.
- [ ] A non-transient git failure is still raised immediately, with no retry — pinned by a test,
      so the marker cannot mask a genuine error.
- [ ] A bundle failure that survives the retries raises an error whose hint describes an
      object-DB read failure rather than a heads conflict.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the s3_doctor + gitutil test tiers pass.
